roadmap.goal: Story #6202: every row of a list longer than 100 rows can be reached, and a short list stays exactly as it is. Frontend only, one slice. Every DataGridBase grid shows MUI's own footer (range and total, e.g. `1–100 of 143`, with previous/next arrows and no rows-per-page choice) only while it is not loading and holds more than 100 rows the reader can see after filters; pages are fixed at 100 and never remembered. The hidePagination prop goes, so Third-party packages follows the same rule, and its search sends the list back to page 1. Export and Copy keep taking every row in sort order. RefinementGrid's enough-for line is placed by the row's position in the whole list, not on the page. Done when zero `it.skip` / `test.skip` remain in the five DISTILL files (DataGridBase.paging.test.tsx, ThirdPartyPackagesSection.paging.test.tsx, RefinementView.paging.test.tsx, WorkItemsDialog.paging.test.tsx, ThirdPartyPackagesPaging.spec.ts): 33 pending cases (32 Vitest, 1 Playwright). The 9 pins stay green, the RowRangeFooter scaffold marker is gone, `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` are green with zero warnings, and the walking skeleton passes locally on both of its branches: a build serving the real SBOMs (more than 100 packages) and one serving the committed placeholders (2 packages).

The crafter writes no new Vitest specifications. Every pending case was written by DISTILL and is skipped. RED means un-skipping it and capturing the failure before the production edit. GREEN is the production code. Three steps (01-02, 01-03 and part of 01-05) un-skip cases that MUI's own behaviour, or an earlier step, already satisfies. Those steps say so, and each such case is shown to be falsifiable once by a temporary sabotage that is reverted, never committed. user_decisions: D1: the footer appears only when a grid has more than 100 rows the reader can see (after filters). With 100 or fewer the grid looks exactly as today, with no footer bar at all.
D2: fixed pages of 100. The footer is MUI's range and total plus previous/next arrows (`1–100 of 243  ‹ ›`). No rows-per-page picker, nothing persisted.
D3: Settings → Third-party packages follows the same rule. Its always-on footer and its picker go.
D4: every DataGridBase consumer in one slice. Conditional footer chosen over virtualised scrolling.
D6: CSV export and Copy keep exporting every row in the current sort order, whichever page is open.
D7 / D8: no DEVOPS wave, no usage-data event.

MD-1 (maintainer, option a): a search in Third-party packages sends the list back to page 1 even when more than 100 rows remain. It is done in ThirdPartyPackagesSection only, and DataGridBase keeps MUI's page policy.

MD-2 (maintainer, option a): RefinementGrid's enough-for line sits where it falls in the whole list, with nothing added. With 143 Work Items: 20 needed → under row 20 on page 1, nothing on page 2. 120 needed → no line on page 1, line under row 120 on page 2. 150 needed → under row 143 with 'All 143 Work Items in Refinement are needed before the next Refinement.'

Engineering (roadmap review H-1, coordinator): the committed SBOM placeholders hold one component each and CI copies the real SBOMs in on main builds only, so the walking skeleton reads how many packages the build serves. At 100 or fewer it asserts the short-list look (no range, no arrows) and stops with an annotation saying why. Above 100 it runs the full paging and search flow.
out_of_scope: Virtualised scrolling without pages, a rows-per-page picker, remembering the page across visits, server-side paging.
Whether Export should honour an active column filter (a separate item for the maintainer). Export behaviour is not changed.
The failure looks of consumers that show their empty message after a failed load (a follow-up the maintainer files; paging does not widen it).
FeatureGrid's 'Select all' keeps selecting every sorted, filtered row on every page.
Regenerating settings/systeminfo.png (it changes: the picker goes), docs, website grep and release-notes line: finalize owns them.
Committing real SBOMs into Lighthouse.Frontend/public/sbom, or changing how CI provides them on PR builds.
Mutation testing (Stryker, with the three new Vitest files in the runner's include: list), refactor passes, review and finalize: the orchestrator runs those after the steps below.
Any backend, API, RBAC, client or usage-data change.

steps.implementation_notes: Mechanism, as DESIGN chose it: DataGridBase stops passing hideFooter and passes a footer slot. The slot renders nothing unless the grid is not loading and its filtered top-level row count is above the page size, and otherwise renders MUI's own GridFooter. Read the count from grid state (the filtered row count or the page count selector, plus the root props' loading), never from rows.length. A column filter does not change rows, so rows.length would leave a dead footer under a filtered list (01-02 pins that). Merge the slot as `{ ...slots, footer }` and keep the merged object referentially stable (useMemo over slots), so RefinementGrid's own row slot survives. Set `pageSizeOptions={[PAGE_SIZE]}` and leave the page size at MUI's default of 100: one option hides both the select and its label. Set hideFooterSelectedRowCount, so keyboard selection never puts '1 row selected' beside the range. No localeText override: the range copy is MUI's. The decision lives in the footer file, and DataGridBase's render body gains no branching (about four changed lines). That keeps the merge with story #6248, which also edits DataGridBase.tsx and types.ts next to `defaultColumnVisibilityModel`, to adjacent hunks. Merge, never overwrite, and never rebase on your own initiative. The crafter may rename RowRangeFooter; PAGE_SIZE is one piece of knowledge used twice, as the page size and as the threshold. This step removes the `__SCAFFOLD__` export and the throwing body, and removes hidePagination from types.ts and DataGridBase (01-06's slice gate greps for both). Removing the prop forces removing `hidePagination={false}` from ThirdPartyPackagesSection.tsx in the same commit (tsc), and that flips the three Third-party packages D3 cases, so they are un-skipped here rather than later. If the line in DataGridBase.test.tsx that credits virtualisation for the 200-row case is touched, reword it to say a page holds 100. Sizing: 10 cases is over the eight-case guide. All ten turn on one predicate (not loading and more than one page) and on the one prop removal that tsc forces into the same commit. Splitting would mean keeping an unused prop for a step, which Biome and Sonar (S6767) reject. PROJECT RULES: read docs/ci-learnings.md first and pre-apply its frontend rules: no negated condition in a ternary (S7735), so write the visibility check positively; cognitive complexity under 15 (S3776); no declared-but-unused prop (S6767); globalThis over window (S7764); pass a single-argument function straight to .map (S7770); `dataset` over getAttribute('data-…') (S7761); a literal used three or more times in one file becomes a constant (S1192); a presence regex starts with ^ or a literal word (S8786). Pin user-visible copy against the literal with the en dash, never a string built from PAGE_SIZE (self-satisfying). RTL regex name matchers are unanchored substring matches: use the exact strings 'Go to next page' / 'Go to previous page' and anchor every regex. Un-skip by `it.skip` → `it` and `it.skip.each` → `it.each`; never add describe.skip (Vitest still evaluates its body). Comments are rare, say the why in plain language, and never cite internal ids such as DDD-3, MD-1, AC-1.6, V13 or D3. Gates: in this worktree run `pnpm install` in Lighthouse.Frontend first and check `pnpm biome --version` against package.json (a stale node_modules runs an old Biome). `pnpm build`'s prebuild runs `biome check --write`, so re-read `git diff` after the build and commit what it rewrote. Never pipe a gate's output through tail or head. Commit: `feat(datagrid): a list longer than 100 rows shows its range and pages (story 6202)`

steps.implementation_notes: Why this is needed: MUI hands the row slot the row's whole-list index, but the spacing callback's index and both 'last visible' flags only cover the current page. So the space for the line and the line drawn by the row disagree once a list pages: there is a blank gap on page 2, and page 1 says all 100 are needed while 143 exist. This is not a new product rule. The line already follows 'the row that makes up the number needed', and that row has one position in the whole list. Recommended mechanism (crafter's choice): DataGridBase turned paging on, so it absorbs paging's effect on its own getRowSpacing prop. It hands the consumer whole-list facts (index = page start + position on the page; last = the filtered list's last row) through a Lighthouse-owned parameter shape, structurally like ShownRow { index, isLastShown } in enoughForPlacement.ts. That narrows getRowSpacing's type in types.ts, next to story #6248's hunk, so merge carefully. The row judges 'last shown' against the filtered row count from grid state, not MUI's page-relative flag. Why RefinementGrid.tsx is in this step: it is the only getRowSpacing caller, and it hands both the row slot and the spacing callback to DataGridBase, so the callback it passes changes when the parameter shape changes. If enoughForPlacement.ts's ShownRow shape is reused or adjusted, it joins this step too (DESIGN lists it as a conditional EXTEND). Allowed alternative: keep MUI's type and convert to whole-list facts inside the Refinement folder, as long as spacing and line share one basis; then DataGridBase.tsx and types.ts drop out of this step. On the Jonas case: the rendered row showing his Yes is the behaviour the reader sees. The castVote check is the contract at the port where the vote leaves the tab. Keep both. The 36px gap stays a literal in the tests: EnoughForLine.tsx's LINE_HEIGHT_PX is module-private, and a literal in one test is clearer than a constant exported only for a test. steps.name: Walking skeleton: Third Party Packages pages on a build with more than 100 packages, and stays a short list on one with fewer; slice gates
steps.description: Give the walking skeleton two branches, chosen by how many packages the build serves. Prove the long branch locally on a build carrying main's real SBOMs and the short branch on the committed placeholders, then un-skip it and run the slice gates.
steps.scenario_name: A long list shows its range, pages to the rest, and a search opens its first page @walking_skeleton @driving_port @us-01 @kpi-OUT-6202-no-hidden-rows @contract-shape:bounded-change
unskips: ThirdPartyPackagesPaging.spec.ts :: A long list shows its range, pages to the rest, and a search opens its first page @walking_skeleton @driving_port @us-01 @kpi-OUT-6202-no-hidden-rows @contract-shape:bounded-change
criteria: The spec first counts the packages the build serves from the SBOMs themselves, never from the grid under test: it fetches /sbom/backend.cdx.json and /sbom/frontend.cdx.json and counts their components with the same filter ThirdPartyPackagesSection applies (name the filter in a comment). The grid's aria-rowcount may be used only as a cross-check that must agree with that count. At 100 or fewer (short branch) the spec asserts that the rows shown equal the SBOM count and that there is no range text and no 'Go to next page' button, so a dropped-row fault fails; it adds a Playwright annotation saying the build serves too few packages to page (the committed placeholder SBOMs) and stops. Above 100 (long branch) it asserts the range total equals the SBOM count and runs the full flow.

Residual risk, stated in the spec header and the commit body: PR CI builds serve the placeholder SBOMs, so in PR CI the walking skeleton proves only the short-list look; the long-list paging is proven in CI by the component tests and in a browser by this step's local real-SBOM run and by CI on main, which builds with the real SBOMs.

Long branch, on a local build carrying main's real SBOMs: the package count is confirmed above 100 before any paging step. Page 1 reads `1–100 of N` with no rows-per-page choice. Page 2 reads `101–…` and its first package differs from page 1's. A search chosen from the real data that leaves more than 100 packages opens `1–100 of …`. The spec comment names the term and the count it left on that run, in plain words.
Short branch, on a local build of the committed placeholders: the spec passes through the short-list assertions and records its annotation.

The spec header no longer claims every real build has well over 100 packages; it says main builds carry the real SBOMs and other builds carry placeholders. The 'Skipped until the paging footer is built' line is gone.
SystemInfoPage.ts gains the package-count member the branch needs. Its existing members are untouched, so the System Info screenshot test still compiles.

While 01-06 runs on the real-SBOM build, a search with a sort and a column filter active is checked by hand: the list opens on page 1, and the sort and filter are kept (01-04's criterion). The result is recorded in the commit body.

steps.implementation_notes: Why two branches: Lighthouse.Frontend/public/sbom/backend.cdx.json and frontend.cdx.json are committed placeholders holding one component each. CI copies the real SBOM artifact over them only when sbom-version is set, which ci.yml does on refs/heads/main only. So PR builds, Renovate PRs included, run ci_verifysqlite / ci_verifypostgres with 2 packages, and a long-only spec would fail there. Count source: the branch must not be chosen by the footer it is testing, or a broken footer would send the spec into the short branch and pass. Read the grid's own row count (for example its `aria-rowcount`, after proving on the live run that it counts every row rather than the page), or the two SBOM endpoints counted with the same filter ThirdPartyPackagesSection applies to components. Whichever you choose, check it against the range total on the real-SBOM run. Never commit a spec or POM member that has not run against a live Lighthouse: DISTILL only type-checked this one. Build and serve from THIS worktree with absolute paths; relative paths in subagents resolve to the main checkout. Run `pnpm install` in /storage/repos/Lighthouse/.claude/worktrees/shimmering-brewing-flute/Lighthouse.Frontend and in .../Lighthouse.EndToEndTests if node_modules is missing. Real SBOMs for the long branch: `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --status success --limit 1 --json databaseId` gives the run id; the version is not in that listing, so read the artifact name from `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/<id>/artifacts --jq '.artifacts[].name'` (it is Lighthouse-SBOM-<version>), then `gh run download <id> --name Lighthouse-SBOM-<version>` downloads into a fresh directory under the session scratchpad. Copy the two .cdx.json files over Lighthouse.Frontend/public/sbom, then run `pnpm build`. `pnpm build` writes into the backend's web root (vite.config.ts `outDir: '../Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend/wwwroot'`), so check that Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend/wwwroot/index.html exists afterwards and that `/sbom/frontend.cdx.json` on the instance serves the real file. Afterwards run `git checkout -- Lighthouse.Frontend/public/sbom` and never commit the real SBOMs. Then rebuild on the placeholders and run the spec once more for the short branch. Start a throw-away backend on 5199 in the background, from /storage/repos/Lighthouse/.claude/worktrees/shimmering-brewing-flute/Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend: `env ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development Kestrel__Endpoints__Http__Url=http://localhost:5199 Kestrel__Endpoints__Https__Url=https://localhost:7299 Database__Provider=sqlite Database__ConnectionString="Data Source=$E2E_DIR/lighthouse.db" Encryption__KeyStorePath=$E2E_DIR/keys UsageData__CollectorBaseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:9 dotnet run --no-launch-profile`, with E2E_DIR a fresh directory under the session scratchpad. Verify each config key against Lighthouse.Backend before using it. The instance time zone is not needed for this page, so leave it out. If you keep it, the key LighthouseClock.cs names in its error message is `Lighthouse:TimeZone` (env `Lighthouse__TimeZone`); confirm where Program.cs reads it first. ASPNETCORE_URLS is ignored here; override the Kestrel keys. Never aim at :5169 (the dev instance). Never point a key store at `data-protection-keys`. Confirm with `ss -ltn | grep 5199`. No premium licence is needed for this page. Then, from the worktree's Lighthouse.EndToEndTests, run `env LIGHTHOUSEURL=http://localhost:5199/ TZ=Europe/Zurich pnpm exec playwright test tests/specs/settings/ThirdPartyPackagesPaging.spec.ts`, then the settings folder with `--grep-invert "@screenshot|@auth|@rbac|@proxyauth"`. Restart the backend after each rebuild so it serves the new web root. Do not regenerate settings/systeminfo.png here: it changes because the picker goes, and finalize deletes and regenerates it. Report, without blocking, the browser checks DESIGN left open: after › is the new page's first row in view; does a shrinking reload show a briefly wrong page; do the range and arrows fit in the Work Items dialog at its smallest width. A defect there becomes a polish step the orchestrator adds. If a briefly wrong page shows, 01-02's controlled-page fallback applies. Stop the backend afterwards. PROJECT RULES: read docs/ci-learnings.md first and pre-apply its Playwright rules: drive the page only through the page object, never an inline page.locator() in the spec; scope locators to the Third Party Packages card so another list's pager never matches; getByRole/getByText names are case-insensitive substrings unless exact, so anchor the range regex; a POM getter that reads 0 or '' while not yet rendered makes a one-sided assertion vacuous, so wait for the first package row before counting. Un-skip with `test.skip` → `test`; never add describe.skip. Comments are rare, plain-language why only, and never cite internal ids such as L-5, MD-1 or AC-1.5. Biome-clean, `pnpm build` zero warnings; its prebuild runs `biome check --write`, so re-read `git diff` afterwards. Never pipe a gate's output through tail or head.
